case_results.prompt:
Run a declawed pass on this paragraph:

It's worth noting that our platform doesn't just streamline workflows, it
fundamentally reimagines them. From startups to enterprises, teams leverage
our robust, scalable, and intuitive tooling to unlock unprecedented value in
today's ever-evolving landscape. What do you think?
case_results.response:
**Scan findings (Phase 1)**

| Category | Count | Worst example |
|---|---|---|
| Puffery / inflated vocabulary | 3 | "unlock unprecedented value in today's ever-evolving landscape" |
| Negative parallelism | 1 | "doesn't just streamline workflows, it fundamentally reimagines them" |
| Hedging / throat-clearing | 1 | "It's worth noting that" |
| False range + rule-of-three | 1 | "From startups to enterprises" / "robust, scalable, and intuitive" |
| Engagement bait | 1 | "What do you think?" |

**Triage:** the "doesn't just X, it Y" sentence decorates an empty claim, so the negation goes and the plain claim stays. "From startups to enterprises" has no meaningful midpoint as written — named the two ends instead. The triplet collapses to the one property the copy can actually stand behind. Puffery and the closing question assert nothing; deleted. No numbers exist in the source, so the specificity gap is flagged rather than invented.

**Rewrite**

> Our platform streamlines workflows. The same tooling serves a startup and a company-wide rollout, and it holds up under both.
> [ADD: one concrete result — hours saved per week, steps cut from a release?]

```
Changes
- Puffery: 3 fixed (deleted; "unlock unprecedented value in today's ever-evolving landscape" carried no claim)
- Negative parallelism: 1 fixed (deleted X half, asserted the plain claim)
- Hedging: 1 fixed (deleted "It's worth noting that")
- False range: 1 fixed (named both ends instead of a range)
- Rule-of-three: 1 fixed (kept the strongest item, cut "robust" and "intuitive")
- Engagement bait: 1 fixed (deleted "What do you think?")
- Cadence: short opening claim, longer second sentence
- Verify passes: 1 (clean)
- Flagged for author: [ADD: one concrete result — hours saved per week, steps cut from a release?]
```

The rewrite is much shorter because roughly two-thirds of the original was frame with no claim inside it. If you want it to fill the original length, it needs a real fact — a number, a customer, a before/after.

case_results.prompt:
Deslop this for a product blog post:

Studies show that many companies struggle with deployment velocity. Our
latest release doesn't just help -- it transforms the picture. In our own
testing, median deploy time fell from 42 minutes to 9 minutes across 14
customer environments. Research suggests this kind of gain is rare.
case_results.response:
**Rewrite**

> In our own testing, the latest release cut median deploy time from 42 minutes to 9 minutes across 14 customer environments.

That one sentence is the whole paragraph's content. Everything else was scaffolding around it.

If you want a lead-in before the number, it has to come with a source:

> [ADD: real source for "companies struggle with deploy velocity" — e.g. DORA State of DevOps, with year and stat.] In our own testing, the latest release cut median deploy time from 42 minutes to 9 minutes across 14 customer environments.

**Changes**
- Low specificity: 2 cut ("Studies show that many companies" and "Research suggests this kind of gain is rare" — both cite nothing and are unfalsifiable; the second also just re-praises the number you already gave)
- Negative parallelism: 1 fixed ("doesn't just help -- it transforms the picture" — deleted; nobody claims a release "just helps", and the 42→9 figure makes the point better than the framing did)
- Puffery: 1 cut ("transforms the picture")
- Cadence: 4 sentences down to 1; the original alternated at a metronomic 8–18 words
- Verify passes: 1 (remaining hit is the 42→9 range — real measured before/after, kept)
- Flagged for author: the optional `[ADD: …]` lead-in source above

One content flag, not style: "in our own testing" plus "14 customer environments" reads oddly — if those are real customer environments, "in our own testing" undersells it; if they're your replicas of customer setups, say so, because a reader will assume the former.

case_results.prompt:
This is a reply I'm about to post on r/devops. Make it not sound like AI.

**Great question!** Here's my take on migrating to Kubernetes:

- **Start small**: Don't just lift and shift, containerise incrementally.
- **Observability matters**: It's not merely about metrics, it's about traces too.
- **Culture is key**: This isn't a tooling change, it's a mindset shift.

Hope this helps! Let me know if you have any questions.
case_results.response:
Ran the declawed loop on it. Scan flagged: stock opener ("Great question!"), engagement-bait sign-off, bold-in-prose plus term:definition bullets (both reddit tells), one "not merely X, it's Y", and the "culture is key" puffery.

**Rewrite:**

> Containerise one service at a time rather than lifting the whole thing over in one go.
>
> Metrics alone stop being useful pretty fast here. Get tracing in from the start — the first time a request dies somewhere between six pods, you'll want it.
>
> And leave time for the people part. Standing up the cluster is the easy half; getting a team to actually think in terms of desired state and ephemeral pods takes a lot longer.

Changes
- Stock skeleton: 2 fixed (deleted the "Great question!" opener and the "Hope this helps! Let me know…" close — both read as assistant, not commenter)
- Negative parallelism: 3 fixed ("don't just lift and shift" → positive instruction; "not merely metrics, traces too" → stated as a plain claim with a reason; "isn't a tooling change, it's a mindset shift" → concrete version of the same point)
- Puffery: 2 fixed ("Observability matters", "Culture is key" → cut the labels, kept the advice)
- Formatting: bold + bulleted term:definition list → plain paragraphs (bold bullets are the biggest AI giveaway in a reddit reply)
- Cadence: varied, 7–26 words, no metronomic run
- Verify passes: 2
- Flagged for author: "desired state and ephemeral pods" and "six pods" are my concretisations of your vaguer "mindset shift" / "traces too" — swap in whatever actually bit you, it'll land better than my guess.
